title: Monthly Ad Revenue by Cohort Month
prompt: You are analyzing ad revenue for a free-to-play mobile game. The `player_sessions` table records every game session with a timestamp and ad impressions shown. The `players` table tracks when each player first signed up. Write a query that groups players into monthly signup cohorts (using the FIRST day of the month they signed up) and calculates total ad revenue per cohort-month. Each ad impression generates $0.02 in revenue. Return columns `cohort_month` (DATE, the first day of the signup month), `total_players` (count of distinct players in that cohort), and `total_ad_revenue` (NUMERIC(10,2), sum of all ad revenue from sessions by players in that cohort). Order results by `cohort_month` ascending. Use DATE_TRUNC to bucket signup dates into monthly cohorts.
schema_ddl: CREATE TABLE players (player_id INT PRIMARY KEY, username VARCHAR(50), signup_date DATE); CREATE TABLE player_sessions (session_id INT PRIMARY KEY, player_id INT, session_start TIMESTAMP, ad_impressions INT);

composite_moves: join players and player_sessions on player_id

hints: You need to combine player signup dates with their session ad impressions, then group by a monthly cohort.
Use DATE_TRUNC('month', signup_date) to bucket each player into the first day of their signup month, then join to sessions and aggregate.

Join players to player_sessions on player_id, compute DATE_TRUNC('month', signup_date)::date AS cohort_month, GROUP BY cohort_month, COUNT(DISTINCT player_id), SUM(ad_impressions * 0.02) with NUMERIC casting, ORDER BY cohort_month.
answer_key: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', p.signup_date)::date AS cohort_month, COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_id) AS total_players, SUM(s.ad_impressions * 0.02)::NUMERIC(10,2) AS total_ad_revenue FROM players p JOIN player_sessions s ON p.player_id = s.player_id GROUP BY cohort_month ORDER BY cohort_month;

_meta.scenario: a free-to-play mobile game tracking session length and ad impressions
